system_description.narrative_title: Escalating Iran–Houthi–Saudi confrontation and regional spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapidly intensifying security crisis centered on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Tehran’s diplomatic moves and proxy leverage, and muscular responses or warnings from the US and Gulf states. Described as an open system, the dynamic links kinetic exchanges (missiles, drones), state and non-state actors, diplomatic signaling (UN, talks), and economic channels (oil prices, stock markets, travel advisories); shocks propagate through feedbacks that alter policy choices, market sentiment, and third-party alignments. The system is driven by cross-border strikes, proxy escalation, external power posturing, and domestic politics, producing high risk of wider regional contagion.
system_description.scope: Military and political interactions among Iran, the Houthis, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, the United States (and its allies), plus associated energy and financial market reactions, travel/security advisories, diplomatic moves at forums like the UN, and near‑term weapon procurements and deployments.
system_description.super_system: The broader Middle East regional security order embedded in the global geopolitical and energy system.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil and financial markets (energy prices, Tadawul and Gulf stocks)
U.S. domestic politics and UN diplomacy (election-driven signaling, summit diplomacy)
Gulf economic/financial integration and partnerships (currency platforms, China ties)
Yemen internal conflict and humanitarian crisis (Houthis, displacement, territorial control)

variables.name: Kinetic attack intensity
variables.description: The aggregate frequency and destructive power of cross-border missile, drone, and direct-kinetic strikes in the theater.

variables.name: Proxy force capability
variables.description: The combat strength, logistical sustainment, and operational reach of irregular or proxy armed groups active in the region.

variables.name: External military posturing
variables.description: The scale and tempo of visible force deployments, patrols, and show-of-force operations by external armed actors around the conflict zone.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement rate
variables.description: The rate and intensity of formal and informal diplomatic contacts, negotiations, and public signaling among relevant actors.

variables.name: Air defense capability
variables.description: The readiness, coverage, and effectiveness of integrated air-defense systems protecting population centers and critical infrastructure.

variables.name: Maritime trade disruption level
variables.description: The current degree to which shipping routes, ports, and maritime commerce are interrupted by insecurity or interdiction.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: The magnitude of short-term price swings and trading volatility in energy commodities driven by security and supply uncertainty.

variables.name: Oil supply disruption
variables.description: The rate at which physical crude oil and refined product availability is reduced or rerouted due to security incidents or blockades.

variables.name: Financial market risk premium
variables.description: The elevation of risk pricing in equity, bond, and currency markets reflecting perceived geopolitical risk in the region.

variables.name: Travel and security advisory level
variables.description: The prevailing intensity of public warnings, travel restrictions, and private-sector risk assessments affecting movement to and within the region.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The strength of internal political demands, protest activity, and public opinion pushing leaders toward restraint or retaliation.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion strength
variables.description: The degree of strategic alignment, burden-sharing, and unified policy among partner actors coordinating responses to the crisis.

variables.name: Arms procurement rate
variables.description: The speed and volume at which actors acquire, transfer, or deploy weapons, munitions, and enabling military systems.

variables.name: Human displacement rate
variables.description: The flow of civilians relocating or fleeing conflict-affected areas per unit time due to insecurity and damage to livelihoods.

variables.name: Intelligence sharing level
variables.description: The depth, timeliness, and operational integration of actionable information exchanged among security actors.

variables.name: Escalation propensity
variables.description: The systemic likelihood that localized incidents will trigger reciprocal responses and broaden into higher‑intensity or wider conflict.

catalysts.title: UN General Assembly high-level meetings
catalysts.description: Leaders' arrivals and high-level meetings in New York (UNGA week) concentrate diplomatic engagement and high-profile signaling among Iran, US, Gulf states.
catalysts.rationale: Iran president to head to New York; Trump set for whirlwind UN meetings; high-level UN engagements.

catalysts.title: Possible US–Iran bilateral at UN
catalysts.description: Open US willingness to meet Iran at the UN could produce a scheduled bilateral or at-ministerial exchange, altering tensions and markets.
catalysts.rationale: US open to meeting Iran at UN; Trump says talks with Iran continue.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi missile/drone campaign
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi targets (capital, airports, fuel depots) are likely to persist and drive cross-border kinetic activity.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis launch missiles at Saudi capital; assault intensifies; claims after fuel depot blaze.

catalysts.title: UK/Turkey military support to Saudi deployments
catalysts.description: Announcements of UK and potential Turkish support for Saudi Arabia point to accelerated deployments, training, or equipment transfers to the theatre.
catalysts.rationale: UK to provide military support to Saudi Arabia; Turkey says it could help meet Saudi military needs.

catalysts.title: Saudi deployment/use of Chinese missiles
catalysts.description: Evidence of Saudi firing of a Chinese missile suggests further deployment or procurement of new strike capabilities, changing strike calculus.
catalysts.rationale: Debris found suggests Saudi Arabia fired its first Chinese missile; implies new weapons employment.

catalysts.title: Negotiations over Strait of Hormuz reopening and land-route trade
catalysts.description: Iran's submission of conditions for reopening Hormuz and activation of land routes indicate an active negotiation and trade-bypass process with uncertain outcomes.
catalysts.rationale: Iran submits conditions for reopening Hormuz; activates land routes to bypass US blockade.

catalysts.title: Houthi push in Yemen highlands and displacement
catalysts.description: Houthi offensive to control Yemen highlands is likely to accelerate civilian flight and reshape local operational reach of the movement.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands; Yemenis flee the Houthi advance.

catalysts.title: Rising travel advisories and market volatility
catalysts.description: Official travel warnings and investor reactions to strikes and rhetoric will lift advisories and risk premia, affecting tourism and financial markets.
catalysts.rationale: U.S. urges Americans to reconsider Middle East travel; Gulf stocks and oil markets fall after Houthi claims.

catalysts.title: Gulf states push for diplomatic reset with Iran
catalysts.description: Calls by Gulf states for a 'reset' with Iran signal coordinated regional diplomacy that could open backchannels and alter alliances.
catalysts.rationale: Gulf states urge reset with Iran as conflict drags on; regional diplomacy intensifies.
